reference: Seven round-trip-result parity cases compare the final decoded bytes and private filesystem results of each implementation encoding and decoding its own data. GNU gzip/xz/bzip2/zstd and Python standard-library zlib provide the separate reference paths; those cases do not establish cross-decoding. Fixed decoder contracts below use byte vectors authored independently of candidate encoders: Python standard-library gzip/zlib/lzma/bz2 streams and a pre-existing independently authored raw-block Zstandard frame. Expected binary payload bytes are explicit base64 contracts. Gzip integrity-error cases retain identical-input GNU output/status parity.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata and unsupported-format rejection.
Seven round-trip-result parity cases cover gzip, concatenated gzip, RFC 1950, raw DEFLATE, XZ, bzip2 and Zstandard; each side decodes its own encoded data.
Private fixture operations and final decoded mode/content parity; compressed artifacts are removed before tree comparison.
Fixed independently authored gzip, concatenated-gzip, RFC 1950 and raw-DEFLATE decoder vectors with binary payloads.
Fixed Python standard-library XZ/bzip2 decoder vectors and an independently authored binary Zstandard raw-block frame.
Identical fixed gzip truncation/CRC inputs, streamed error output and same-shell write-error recovery.
exclusions: Compressed stream bytes are not asserted identical; codec headers and compressor choices may vary. Round trips and decoded bytes are compared, and temporary compressed artifacts are removed before tree comparison.
Deterministic short-write, zero-write and EINTR injection remain deferred pending a reviewed mock. Ordinary closed-output-descriptor failure and same-shell recovery are covered without a mock.
A parity case is skipped by the runner if its named GNU/reference executable is unavailable.

The seven round-trip-result cases do not assert candidate encoder interoperability or compressed-byte identity. Fixed vectors qualify only the stated decoder inputs; exhaustive codec options, block types, windows and header variations remain outside scope.

cases.purpose: Confirm the loadable is registered as a Bash builtin using Bash's type metadata.
Check the help contract advertises the multi-format command and the documented RFC 1950 and concatenated-gzip behavior.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help zlib)
[[ $help_text == *'Multi-format compression / decompression'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'RFC 1950 (raw zlib wrap, NOT gzip)'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'Gzip decode handles concatenated (multi-member) .gz files.'* ]]
printf 'documented-help-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Compare final binary round-trip results and private fixture operations. The candidate encoder feeds its own decoder; the GNU encoder feeds the GNU decoder. No cross-decoding or compressed-byte identity is claimed by this case.
cases.script:
mkdir -p fixture/source fixture/archive
printf 'header\000middle\377tail\n' > fixture/source/payload
chmod 640 fixture/source/payload
cp fixture/source/payload fixture/archive/copy
mv fixture/archive/copy fixture/archive/input
touch fixture/archive/marker
if [[ $(type -t zlib) == builtin ]]; then
  zlib -e -1 -f gzip fixture/archive/input > fixture/archive/data.gz
  zlib -f gzip fixture/archive/data.gz > fixture/archive/unpacked
else
  gzip -1 -c fixture/archive/input > fixture/archive/data.gz
  gzip -dc fixture/archive/data.gz > fixture/archive/unpacked
fi
cmp fixture/archive/input fixture/archive/unpacked
rm fixture/archive/data.gz
cat fixture/archive/unpacked

cases.purpose: Compare final output from two concatenated members encoded and decoded by each implementation separately. This establishes result parity for those round trips, not interoperability between their encoders and decoders.
cases.script:
printf 'first-member\n' > first
printf 'second\000member\n' > second
if [[ $(type -t zlib) == builtin ]]; then
  zlib -e -f gzip first > first.gz
  zlib -e -f gzip second > second.gz
  cat first.gz second.gz > combined.gz
  zlib combined.gz > decoded
else
  gzip -c first > first.gz
  gzip -c second > second.gz
  cat first.gz second.gz > combined.gz
  gzip -dc combined.gz > decoded
fi
cat decoded
rm first.gz second.gz combined.gz

cases.purpose: Compare final RFC 1950 round-trip results: candidate encoding is decoded by the candidate, while Python standard-library encoding is decoded by Python. This case alone does not establish cross-decoding interoperability.
cases.script:
printf 'wrapped\000zlib\377payload\n' > plain
if [[ $(type -t zlib) == builtin ]]; then
  zlib -e -z plain > packed.z
  zlib -z packed.z > decoded
else
  python3 -c 'import sys,zlib; sys.stdout.buffer.write(zlib.compress(sys.stdin.buffer.read()))' < plain > packed.z
  python3 -c 'import sys,zlib; sys.stdout.buffer.write(zlib.decompress(sys.stdin.buffer.read()))' < packed.z > decoded
fi
cmp plain decoded
cat decoded
rm packed.z decoded

cases.purpose: Compare final raw-DEFLATE round-trip results: candidate encoding is decoded by the candidate, while Python standard-library encoding is decoded by Python. Compressed bytes and cross-decoding are not compared here.
cases.script:
printf 'raw\000deflate\377payload\n' > plain
if [[ $(type -t zlib) == builtin ]]; then
  zlib -e -R plain > packed.deflate
  zlib -R packed.deflate > decoded
else
  python3 -c 'import sys,zlib; c=zlib.compressobj(wbits=-15); d=sys.stdin.buffer.read(); sys.stdout.buffer.write(c.compress(d)+c.flush())' < plain > packed.deflate
  python3 -c 'import sys,zlib; sys.stdout.buffer.write(zlib.decompress(sys.stdin.buffer.read(),-15))' < packed.deflate > decoded
fi
cmp plain decoded
cat decoded
rm packed.deflate decoded

cases.purpose: Compare final binary round-trip results from candidate XZ encode/decode and external xz encode/decode. Each implementation reads its own encoded stream in this case.
cases.script:
printf 'xz\000container\377payload\n' > plain
if [[ $(type -t zlib) == builtin ]]; then
  zlib -e -f xz plain > packed.xz
  zlib -f xz packed.xz > decoded
else
  xz -c plain > packed.xz
  xz -dc packed.xz > decoded
fi
cmp plain decoded
cat decoded
rm packed.xz decoded

cases.purpose: Compare final binary round-trip results from candidate bzip2 encode/decode and external bzip2 encode/decode. Each implementation reads its own encoded stream in this case.
cases.script:
printf 'bzip2\000block\377payload\n' > plain
if [[ $(type -t zlib) == builtin ]]; then
  zlib -e -f bzip2 plain > packed.bz2
  zlib -f bzip2 packed.bz2 > decoded
else
  bzip2 -c plain > packed.bz2
  bzip2 -dc packed.bz2 > decoded
fi
cmp plain decoded

cases.purpose: Compare final binary round-trip results from candidate Zstandard encode/decode and external zstd encode/decode. Each implementation reads its own encoded stream; quiet mode suppresses only external progress messages.
cases.script:
printf 'zstandard\000frame\377payload\n' > plain
if [[ $(type -t zlib) == builtin ]]; then
  zlib -e -f zstd plain > packed.zst
  zlib -f zstd packed.zst > decoded
else
  zstd -q -c plain > packed.zst
  zstd -q -dc packed.zst > decoded
fi
cmp plain decoded
cat decoded
rm packed.zst decoded

cases.purpose: Decode the same fixed gzip-member prefix on both sides. This isolates partial-output/status parity from optional filename headers and per-encoder framing choices.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x1f\x8b\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\xff\x4b\x2b\xca\xcf' > broken.gz
if [[ $(type -t zlib) == builtin ]]; then
 if zlib -f gzip broken.gz > decoded 2> diagnostic; then decoder_status=0; else decoder_status=$?; fi
else
 if gzip -dc broken.gz > decoded 2> diagnostic; then decoder_status=0; else decoder_status=$?; fi
fi
[[ $decoder_status == 1 && -s diagnostic ]]
printf 'truncated-member-rejected\n'
cat decoded
rm broken.gz decoded diagnostic

cases.purpose: Verify that a format outside the documented gzip/xz/lzma/zstd/bzip2/zlib/deflate set is rejected before reading or emitting a stream.
cases.script:
if zlib -f unsupported </dev/null > result 2> diagnostic; then command_status=0; else command_status=$?; fi
[[ $command_status != 0 ]]
[[ ! -s result ]]
[[ -s diagnostic ]]
rm result diagnostic
printf 'unsupported-format-rejected\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise byte-exact encoding and decoding across deterministic interrupted reads, short writes and zero writes.
cases.reason: Requires a reviewed FD/syscall mock in a future disposable VM to inject EINTR and partial/zero writes deterministically. Ordinary closed-descriptor write failure is covered separately in the private namespace fixture; injected faults are not claimed as passes.

cases.script:

cases.purpose: Independent expected payload bytes survive CRC failure; closed stdout during decode and encode reports failure, then a later invocation decodes normally without leaked mode or codec state.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x1f\x8b\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\xff\x73\x0e\x72\x56\x28\x48\xac\xcc\xc9\x4f\x4c\xe1\x02\x00\xf0\xe8\xec\xd1\x0c\x00\x00\x00' > bad.gz
printf '%b' '\x1f\x8b\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\xff\x4b\x2b\xca\xcf\x55\x28\x2e\x49\xc9\xcc\xe3\x02\x00\x1d\x7c\xde\x4f\x0b\x00\x00\x00' > good.gz
printf 'ordinary payload\n' > plain
rc=0; zlib -f gzip bad.gz > partial 2> diagnostic || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 && -s diagnostic ]]
cat partial
rc=0; zlib -f gzip good.gz 1>&- 2> write-diagnostic || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 && -s write-diagnostic ]]
rc=0; zlib -e -f gzip plain 1>&- 2> encode-diagnostic || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 && -s encode-diagnostic ]]
printf 'write errors recovered\n'
zlib -f gzip good.gz
cases.stdout:
CRC payload
write errors recovered
from stdin

cases.purpose: Decode fixed streams generated with Python standard-library lzma FORMAT_XZ/CHECK_CRC64 and bz2. Independent expected bytes contain NUL and 0xff; the candidate only decodes.

Decode the independently authored five-byte binary Zstandard raw-block frame already qualified against external zstd in the zstdcat fixture. Expected bytes are A, NUL, B, 0xff, LF; no candidate encoding is involved.
